extracted.intended_audience: educated Catholics, theology students, clergy, and readers interested in the relation between physical science and theology
extracted.subtask_description: A lecture-length treatment comparing the methods, subject-matter, and rightful domains of Physics and Theology, arguing for their essential separation and explaining causes of historical conflict. It outlines how each discipline should be conducted and how apparent conflicts should be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of natural and supernatural knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: We may divide knowledge, then, into natural and supernatural... These two great circles of knowledge... intersect; first, as far as supernatural knowledge includes truths and facts of the natural world, and secondly, as far as truths and facts of the natural world are on the other hand data for inferences about the supernatural. Still... the two worlds and the two kinds of knowledge respectively are separated off from each other; and that, therefore, as being separate, they cannot on the whole contradict each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat natural (science) and supernatural (theology) as largely distinct domains; mastery of one does not entitle one to form judgments about the other (e.g., a physicist knows nothing about angels; a divine knows nothing about laws of motion). Allow intersections but do not expect contradiction; do not conflate the fields when assessing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physics confines itself to phenomena and cause-and-effect
rubrics_metrics.description: In Physics is comprised that family of sciences which is concerned with the sensible world... Its basis of operations... is the phenomena which meet the senses. It never travels beyond the examination of cause and effect. Its object is to resolve the complexity of phenomena into simple elements and principles... With matter it began, with matter it will end; it will never trespass into the province of mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep physical inquiry 'extra artem' from questions beyond its method (final causes, ultimate Being, why the universe exists). A physicist should not introduce final causes into physical investigations; asking how the universe is sustained is outside the physicist's professional task. Avoid overreaching physical explanations into theological territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theology begins with the Author and treats final causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Theology begins... with the one invisible, unapproachable Cause and Source of all things. It unfolds and systematizes what He Himself has told us of Himself; of His nature, His attributes, His will, and His acts... The Physicist treats of efficient causes; the Theologian of final. The Physicist tells us of laws; the Theologian of the Author, Maintainer, and Controller of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach theological questions by appeal to revelation and authoritative depositaries; address questions about souls, conscience, destiny, and final causes rather than empirical phenomena. Theology's methods and subject-matter are distinct and should be respected as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each discipline must stick to its proper method
rubrics_metrics.description: The elementary methods of reasoning and inquiring used in Theology and Physics are contrary the one to the other; each of them has a method of its own... neither of them has been quite content to remain on its own homestead, but... each has considered it the best for all purposes and has... attempted to impose it upon the other science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing deductive/theological methods on empirical science and avoid imposing inductive/experimental methods on theology. Both overreaches are errors: theologians converting non-deductive subjects into deductive systems, and experimentalists attempting to make theology an inductive/experimental science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural physical statements require authoritative interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Holy Scripture... does declare a few momentous facts, so few that they may be counted, of a physical character... their meaning has not yet engaged the formal attention of the Church, or received any interpretation which, as Catholics, we are bound to accept, and in the absence of such definite interpretation, there is perhaps some presumption in saying that it means this, and does not mean that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Scripture appears to assert physical claims (e.g., six days of creation, a fixed earth, a great deluge), wait for authoritative ecclesiastical interpretation before declaring conflict with scientific results. Do not treat unofficial or popular interpretations as definitive grounds for dispute with science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Scripture according to unanimous consent of the Fathers and authoritative tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripture, we know, is to be interpreted according to the unanimous consent of the Fathers; but, besides this consent, there have ever been in Christendom a number of floating opinions... to be received at least with attention and deference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the Church's authoritative and unanimous patristic interpretation over popular, long-standing, or speculative readings. Distinguish 'floating' opinions (e.g., millennialism, specific prophetic schedules) from authoritative tradition when using Scripture to adjudicate scientific or historical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Theology (Argument from Design) is distinct from Physics
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a science which avails itself of the phenomena and laws of the material universe... taken the name of Natural Theology... though absolutely distinct from Physics, yet Physical Philosophers, having furnished its most curious and interesting data, are apt to claim it as their own, and to pride themselves upon it accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Natural Theology as a separate discipline that uses physical phenomena as evidence for design, power, wisdom, and goodness of a Creator. Acknowledge the contribution of physical data but resist claims that Natural Theology is merely a branch of Physics; recognize historical continuity of the design argument independent of modern discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: truth cannot be contrary to truth; require convergence among sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth cannot be contrary to truth; if these three subject-matters were able, under the pressure of the inductive method, to yield respectively theological conclusions in unison and in concord with each other, and also contrary to the doctrines of Theology as a deductive science, then that Theology would... be in an anxious position... if these three subject-matters... worked through three centuries by men of great abilities, with the method or instrument of Bacon in their hands, have respectively issued in conclusions contradictory of each other... then that empirical method... has come to no one conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When employing Scripture, Antiquity, and Nature as bases for theological conclusions, expect and require some convergence; widespread divergence among conclusions from these sources undermines the claim that inductive methods have established an alternative theology. Use the 'truth cannot be contrary to truth' principle to caution against premature rejection of doctrinal tradition based on inconclusive or conflicting inductive results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theology is deductive and not progressive like inductive sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The argumentative method of Theology is that of a strict science, such as Geometry, or deductive; the method of Physics... is that of an empirical pursuit, or inductive... From the time of the Apostles to the end of the world no strictly new truth can be added to the theological information which the Apostles were inspired to deliver. It is possible... to make numberless deductions from the original doctrines; but, as the conclusion is ever in its premisses, such deductions are not, strictly speaking, an addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach theological development as elaboration and deduction from revealed premises rather than accumulation of novel empirical truths. Avoid treating theology as a progressive experimental science analogous to mathematics or inductive natural sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inductive theology attempts and its three principal data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: For an experimental science, we must have a large collection of phenomena... Three principal stores have been used... the first, the text of Holy Scripture; the second, the events and transactions of ecclesiastical history; the third, the phenomena of the visible world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one attempts an inductive theology, it must draw on Scripture, antiquity/ecclesiastical history, and natural phenomena. However, exercise caution: historically these sources, when treated inductively, have produced divergent and inconclusive theological systems rather than a single unified result; treat such attempts skeptically and check for internal coherence before accepting novel doctrinal conclusions.
